title: Genome-wide mapping of replication stress response factors reveals the management of polycistronic transcription; replication initiation; and responses to replication stress in Leishmania.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, Europe's sequence repository) for project PRJEB83580 five ways: the project record exists and is flagged PUBLIC (first public 2025-02-28), but read_run, read_experiment, analysis and sample queries all return zero rows, so no FASTQ (raw read) or submitted file is listed. NCBI BioProject 1229983 mirrors the record with sequencing_status 'Unknown' and elink to the Sequence Read Archive returns nothing. The Europe PMC supplementary-file archive timed out on three attempts, so the two supplementary tables could not be opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That ChIP-seq (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing) for gamma-H2A, RPA1 and RAD9 plus whole-genome sequencing were generated; that processing used Bowtie2, SAMtools, MACS2 and deepTools (bamCoverage/bamCompare); that Supplementary Table S1 lists oligonucleotides and S2 is a second small table. No processed coverage tracks, peak tables or count matrices are mentioned as deposited anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: The only new data is the ENA deposit PRJEB83580, and it is empty: the study record is public but contains zero released runs, experiments, samples or analyses, so there is no file to download. No processed tracks or peak coordinates were deposited in any other repository, and the supplementary archive would not retrieve.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Even if the reads appeared, the prediction target (replication-stress-response enrichment per genomic region) exists nowhere as a column; it would have to be constructed by aligning reads, calling peaks with MACS2 and binning coverage, exactly as the authors did in-house.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed beyond noting the Leishmania major reference genome is freely available from TriTrypDB, so DNA sequence inputs would exist if signal data did.

a4_units_stated.note: No data file exists to carry units; the paper describes normalised coverage ratios computed with deepTools but no deposited table states them.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count could be verified because no file is retrievable. The biological unit is also small: a handful of ChIP samples across three proteins and a few stress conditions in one 33 Mb genome.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A 33 Mb parasite genome plus a few ChIP libraries would fit a laptop in principle, but raw sequencing reads are excluded by project policy and nothing is available to size.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: the paper and the ENA record describe ChIP-seq on three proteins, but the repository lists no runs to compare against. The ENA project title also names RAD9 while the published abstract names only gamma-H2A and RPA1.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying signal is a physical measurement (antibody pulldown followed by sequencing), not another model's output, so provenance itself is sound; the problem is that it is unobtainable.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the deposited data for this paper contains no released files.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use local DNA sequence and features to predict where a parasite's genome shows replication-stress damage signals.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered was: for each window of the Leishmania major genome, the DNA sequence plus annotations such as transcription start and stop sites, and predict the measured enrichment of replication-stress-response proteins. Number of usable windows: unknown, because no data file could be opened.
plain_idea.predict: Enrichment of the damage markers gamma-H2A, RPA1 and RAD9 measured by ChIP-seq (pulling down a protein with an antibody and sequencing the DNA attached to it), under normal and stressed growth.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Parasitologists working on Leishmania genome plasticity and drug resistance would want to know whether sequence alone predicts where stress damage lands; but none of it is testable while the repository is empty.

ml_idea: Predict per-window replication-stress-response ChIP-seq signal in Leishmania major from DNA sequence and transcription-unit annotation, with a DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer frozen as a feature extractor. Not executable: the data behind it is not released.

effort.compute_note: No estimate made; the evaluation stopped at the first Part A killer because no data file exists to size or time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query the ENA portal for runs in PRJEB83580 — it returns zero rows, which kills the project in one call.

verdict_reason: ENA project PRJEB83580 is public but holds zero released sequencing runs or files, so the paper's only new data cannot be downloaded (A1). Even if released it would be raw ChIP-seq reads with the prediction target needing full construction by alignment and peak calling (A2), with only a handful of samples in one strain of one species.
